newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares dipped on Monday as a late wave of futures-related selling hit the index and caused it to finish at its day lows, dealers said.
Futures traders took advantage of a wary market to dump stock and drive the index down in the hope of buying back at lower levels.
"There was a lot of futures-related selling at the end," one dealer said.
After the rand-led fall last week all market eyes were nervously fixed on the performance of the ailing currency and the bonds market.
There was no repeat of last week's dramatic swings, but the share market was still nervous enough to lock into a downward path early on.
"There was quite a bit of nervous trade with everyone watching the rand," one dealer said.

The rand ended a quiet day below 4.70 on the dollar after a late offshore dollar sell order hit the market market, while the benchmark R150 bonds was last at 15.920 pct from 15.855 pct overnight in lacklustre trade.
The all-share index ended dropped 18.5 points to end at 6,952.9 as industrials fell 18.8 points to 8,175.3.
Golds did better as shares firmed on a steadier bullion price, though it is still below the important $380 an ounce level. The golds index ended up 9.9 points at 1,732.4.

Some indivdual shares performed well. Electronics group DiData got a good follow through from its results last week and put on 35 cents to 10.90 rand. The positive sentiment saw the electronics sector gain 18.4 points to 3,653.3.

Debut share South African financial services group Forbes Ltd had a good first day's trading. Forbes' stock, listed at 535 cents each, ended trading at 800 cents after touching a day high of 815 cents.
De Beers shed 250 cents to 139.75 rand, Richemont was unmoved at 72.25 rand and SA Breweries ended at 121.50 rand, down 50 cents.
Futures had a quietish day as the December all-share contract was at 6,420/35 from 6,455. The industrials contract eased to 7,856/60 from 7,971 and the gold contract edged up to 1,238/40 from 1,231.
